consensus_summary: A “new name” signifies a God-given transformed identity, status, character, or belonging, whether individual or corporate.
book_summary: The “new name” is the renewed covenant itself, privately known and kept by its recipient.
consensus_core_identification: New name = renewed identity or status bestowed by God.
book_core_identification: New name = renewed covenant received and faithfully kept.
boundary_disagreement: The book does not merely narrow the kinds of transformed identity covered. It reclassifies the symbol’s referent from the recipient’s identity or status to the covenant the recipient receives and keeps.
material_contradiction: Identity/status and covenant are distinct referents. Although covenant renewal may produce a changed identity, identifying the name as the covenant replaces rather than simply specifies the consensus identification.
rationale: The book expressly acknowledges the common identity-and-character interpretation but substitutes “renewed covenant.” The secrecy language overlaps with the common Revelation 2:17 reading, yet it is applied to a different object: a covenant known and kept rather than a personal or bestowed name. Because this is a replacement of the central referent, not merely an unlisted detail, DIVERGENT is more appropriate than NOVEL or REFINED.
strongest_objection: Revelation 2:17 directly says that the name is known only by its recipient, but it does not call the name a covenant or say that it is “kept.” Genesis 32 and Isaiah 62 more directly connect renaming with changed identity, status, and covenantal restoration; they support covenant context but not clearly the equation “new name = renewed covenant.”
